Harvey introductory vortex and cloth, updated 2026-11-09

Implementation: dist/spin-unlock.js, dist/vortex.js, dist/vendor/cloth-sim.js,
dist/wordmark-fragments.js and the return sequence in dist/app.js.
Cloth constraints and damped Verlet integration adapted from
Dmitry Kurash's Holocloth (MIT), src/cloth.ts at commit
a6078ba698a53cbf18be870cea555c1971f84103. License in cloth-LICENSE.txt.
https://github.com/dmitrykurash/holocloth/tree/a6078ba698a53cbf18be870cea555c1971f84103

Visual/technical references consulted:
- Azkun/balatroShader author README:
  https://github.com/Azkun/balatroShader
  Describes centered trigonometric rotation, iterative transformations, palette,
  speed and spin controls in a public browser reconstruction.
- React Bits Balatro component overview:
  https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/balatro
  Demonstrates the swirling paint and crisp pixel treatment.
- EMA Multimedia's HBO DVD opening, from creator Michael Pace's archive:
  https://michaelpace.com/legacy-portfolio/
  The scattered pieces and quick, clean arrival inspired the reveal timing.

This project uses independently written polar coordinates, three bounded
sinusoidal domain-warp passes, green/yellow palette bands and subtle pixel grain.
The gesture controller integrates separate angles for the cloth and paint.
A catch nudges the sheet, while the paint picks up speed from the turning
cloth. A gentle turn carries only part of the sheet's speed into the color.
A hard pull can speed up the paint, which coasts through pauses and reversals.
The grab responds lightly while the first 0.20 radians take up the slack.
The difference between hand and cloth angles builds spring tension. Traction
increases with that tension. A hard pull builds a stronger spring release.
Drag unlock requires 7.2 seconds of movement and 1.1 turns. A new grip can
resume the accumulated progress. Desktop wheel and touchpad input credit
1,000 normalized pixels of scroll travel over at least 4.8 seconds.
A flat resting mesh keeps the original paint colors and fine pixel grain.
Soft lighting appears on the temporary folds.

The 36 orbiting pieces come from the user's original painted letters. The
seams between V, E and Y follow the gaps in the source photo. Turning earns
the assembly. After a letter fits, it holds briefly and flies off screen even
if the user lets go. Its departure and a short gap precede the next letter.
At unlock the intact name returns once from below with its green trail and
the local cheer. The reference videos supply timing inspiration only.
Movement energy modulates the filaments and palette. Reduced motion holds the
flat paint still. The Canvas2D renderer uses the same cloth and depth at a
bounded resolution with precomputed paint textures. WebGL is capped at DPR 1.5
and 1.5M pixels, and Canvas is capped at 115K pixels.

Balatro and its branding belong to their respective owners; this is an original
green/yellow website treatment inspired by its background, not official assets.
